findings.title: Rate-limit and server errors are still reported as an invalid token with re-auth advice.
findings.body: Issue #14053 asks for 401 (invalid or revoked token) to be told apart from other failures such as a 403 rate limit, a 5xx or a network error, so that those no longer print "The token in … is invalid." and "To re-authenticate, run: gh auth refresh". This change keeps that wording and the hint for every error, and only adds an `Error:` line under them. The new tests lock this in: the 403 and 503 cases still expect "The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid." (hunk 11), and the 503 case in hunk 6 still expects the `gh auth refresh` hint. A rate-limited user still gets told to run `gh auth refresh`, which the issue says makes things worse. Fix: when the error is not a 401, show a "Could not verify token: <error>" state and drop the re-auth and logout hints.

findings.title: The new diagnostic only appears when stderr is a TTY, so the CI and agent case in the issue never sees it.
findings.body: The issue's reproduction is an agent or CI loop that uses up the rate limit. In those environments stderr is usually not a terminal, so `opts.IO.IsStderrTTY()` is false. The output then stays exactly as before: "token is invalid" with no underlying error. The non-TTY subtests in `Test_statusRun_errorDiagnostic` confirm that the error is left out. Writing the extra line in non-TTY mode as well would let the people who hit this see the real cause. At the least, the TTY gate should be justified against the request.
